nav.ai.desc: Check the AI apps you want installed. Uncheck one to uninstall it.
nav.androidStudio.desc:
The official integrated development environment for Android apps, now with Gemini in Android Studio, an AI-powered coding companion.

To install Android Studio, download the .tar.gz file from https://developer.android.com/studio
nav.androidStudio.note: The Android Studio installer opens in its own window. In the setup wizard, on the welcome screen or in the main menu, click the gear icon (Configure, or the three-dot menu) and choose "Create Desktop Entry". That adds Android Studio's icon to your system's application menu.
nav.androidStudio.noteUpdate: Use Android Studio itself to update it.
nav.antigravityIDE.desc:
Google Antigravity's editor view offers Tab completion, natural-language code commands and a configurable, context-aware agent.

To install Antigravity IDE (Standalone), download the .tar.gz file from https://antigravity.google/download#antigravity-ide
nav.devFolders.desc: Mount a development folder inside an app container: a plugin in Moodle, or any folder in PHP, Generic, Node and PHP + Node apps.
nav.dockerCreate.desc: Create a new Nginx, MariaDB or app container (Moodle, PHP, Generic, Node or PHP + Node).
nav.dockerManage.desc: Start, stop, restart, recreate, view the logs of, edit or remove Perci82 Dev's Docker containers.
nav.exportImport.desc: Export or import the Docker containers and the mounted development folders, choosing the items.
nav.flatpaks.desc: Check the applications you want installed. Uncheck one to uninstall it.
nav.fonts.desc: Check the fonts you want installed. Uncheck one to uninstall it.
nav.fonts.title: Manage Fonts
nav.ides.desc: Install, update or uninstall each IDE. An IDE that depends on a prerequisite can only be installed after it.
nav.overview.systemDesc: See the detected system and the version of Perci82 System.
nav.prereqs.desc: Install, update or uninstall each prerequisite. The items others require come first; an item that depends on another can only be installed after it.
nav.sdks.desc: Install, update or uninstall each SDK. An SDK that depends on a prerequisite can only be installed after it.
nav.settings.systemDesc: Language, theme and Flatpak installation scope.
nav.templates.desc: Check the file templates you want installed. Uncheck one to remove it.
nav.templates.title: Manage File Templates
nav.terminals.desc:
Check the terminals you want installed. Uncheck one to uninstall it.
Installed terminals get an "Open in <terminal>" entry in the context menu of Nautilus (Scripts submenu), Nemo and Dolphin.
nav.update.desc:
Updates your operating system and applications:
- your distribution's packages
- the Snap packages (when available)
- the user's and the system's Flatpaks (when available)
nav.update.title: Update OS & Apps
path.notPicked: Path not picked in the file chooser: {path}
pi.backportsBudgie.desc: Adds the {ppa} PPA (newer stable Budgie components, maintained by the Ubuntu Budgie team), refreshes the package list and applies the upgrades (apt-get full-upgrade). It replaces core desktop components such as budgie-extras, labwc and wlroots: take a Timeshift snapshot first.
pi.budgieEssentials.desc: Restricted codecs (ubuntu-restricted-extras), build tools, Timeshift and common command-line utilities.
pi.cleanup.desc: Removes orphan dependencies and cleans the dnf cache (autoremove + clean all).
pi.drivers.desc: Runs ubuntu-drivers autoinstall to install the recommended proprietary drivers (e.g. NVIDIA).
pi.enableRepos: Enable the universe and multiverse repositories
pi.enableRepos.desc: Adds Ubuntu's universe and multiverse components, needed by most packages below.
pi.fedoraCodecs.desc: Swaps ffmpeg-free for the full ffmpeg and installs the multimedia group (dnf group install), for common audio/video formats.
pi.fedoraEssentials.desc: Build tools, file compression and common command-line utilities.
pi.fedoraVaapiAMD.desc: Installs hardware video acceleration for AMD GPUs (from RPM Fusion). Only for AMD GPUs.
pi.fedoraVaapiIntel.desc: Installs hardware video acceleration for Intel GPUs (from RPM Fusion). Only for Intel GPUs.
pi.flatpakSetup.desc: Makes sure Flatpak is installed, adds the Flathub repository and installs VLC and a web app shortcut manager.
pi.flatpakWebApps.desc: Makes sure Flatpak is installed, adds the Flathub repository and installs a web app shortcut manager.
pi.mintEssentials.desc: Media codecs, Ubuntu drivers, build tools, an archive manager, Timeshift and common command-line utilities.
pi.msFonts.desc: Installs the ttf-mscorefonts-installer package (accepting its license automatically).
pi.ntfs.desc: Installs ntfs-3g (from the Fedora repositories) to read and write NTFS disks — best effort, the kernel's ntfs3 driver may already cover it.
pi.popCodecs.desc: Installs ubuntu-restricted-extras and gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad (System76's official advice for Pop!_OS).
pi.popEssentials.desc: Build tools, Timeshift and common command-line utilities.
pi.popFlatpak.desc: Installs VLC and a web app shortcut manager from Flathub (already set up on Pop!_OS).
pi.rpmFusion.desc: Adds the RPM Fusion free and nonfree repositories, needed for codecs and video drivers.

pi.unrar.desc: Installs unrar (from RPM Fusion nonfree), to extract .rar files.

prereq.build-essential: C/C++ compilers (GCC) and make — used, for example, by Rust to link programs and by libraries with native code
prereq.curl: Command-line tool for transferring data with URLs
prereq.docker: Docker container engine and the Docker Compose utility. The user is added to the docker group, whose access is equivalent to administrator (root) on the computer.
prereq.flatpak: Package manager and distribution system for sandboxed applications
prereq.flatpak-builder: Tool to build applications in the Flatpak format
prereq.flatpak-builder-tools: Offline source generators to package for Flatpak/Flathub: flatpak-node-generator (npm dependencies, through pipx) and flatpak-cargo-generator.py (Rust dependencies), from ~/tools/flatpak-builder-tools at a fixed commit

prereq.gtk3dev: Header and development files of the GTK 3 library (used, for example, by Flutter Linux desktop apps)
prereq.gtk4dev: Header and development files of the GTK 4 library — needed to build Perci82's own GUI (Wails v3)
prereq.libfuse2: FUSE2 compatibility library, needed to run AppImages
prereq.librsvg: The rsvg-convert utility, to convert SVG images to PNG/PDF (used, for example, to generate icons), and the librsvg headers (used to build Tauri apps)
prereq.libsecret: Utility to reach the system keyring through the Secret Service API (on Fedora, includes git-credential-libsecret, which keeps Git passwords in the keyring)
prereq.libxdo: libxdo headers (keyboard and mouse simulation on X11) — needed to build Tauri v2 apps
prereq.lsof: Utility that lists the files the system has open
prereq.mkcert: Generates locally trusted TLS certificates (used by the Nginx container of the per-project Docker stack)
prereq.node: JavaScript runtime (the LTS version, installed through nvm)
